parts.note: Genesis has Eve made from a bone taken from Adam's side, read here as a cut of meat he could spare

explanation.surface: A question about what Adam contributed to Eve, as if they shared a smoke or an investment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Joint' tempts as a shared venture; it is a butcher's joint, a cut of pork ribs.
explanation.definitionFit: A cut of pork from the ribs is a butcher's joint, and the Bible makes Eve from Adam's rib.

clue.text: Cloth made by: Alec, per haps

parts.note: per is Latin for by, as in 'per post'

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the letters of the name are only a possible arrangement, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A note that some fabric may have been made by a man called Alec.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' turns ALEC into CALE, after PER for 'by'.
explanation.definitionFit: Percale is a closely woven cotton fabric used for bed sheets.

definitions.meaning: a library whose books are consulted on the spot, not lent out
a written testimonial to someone's character, as an employer gives

explanation.definitionFit: A reference library holds dictionaries and encyclopedias for consultation, and a reference is a testimonial vouching for someone's character.

clue.text: They're left when the slicer breaks down

indicators.note: something that breaks down falls apart, so the letters of slicer are reassembled

explanation.surface: Bits left behind when a kitchen slicing machine fails.
explanation.definitionFit: Relics are remains, things surviving from the past.

clue.text: B.I.M. greets banana combine in low place for a cheap deal

definitions.text: low place for a cheap deal

indicators.note: to combine is to mix together, so all these letters are blended into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone called B.I.M. hails a banana cartel down in the cellar, where deals are cheap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'combine' looks like a noun (a business cartel) but is the anagram signal on BIM GREETS BANANA.
explanation.definitionFit: A store's basement floor often holds discounted goods, so it is a low-down spot for bargains.

definitions.meaning: the Pump Room at Bath serves spa water raised from the spring, so whimsically it is in that room

explanation.definitionFit: To pump someone is to question them hard, and the famous Pump Room in Bath, a spa city in England, is a fanciful second sense.

parts.note: p, piano, is the musical direction for playing quietly
rattled means unsettled or disconcerted

explanation.surface: Someone, quietly thrown off balance, babbled like a child.
explanation.definitionFit: To prattle is to chatter in a silly, infantile way.

clue.text: Attitude in a rough spot on the river

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece sits on top of the next
rough suggests something roughed up or knocked about, so the letters are shuffled

parts.note: the Ure is a river in Yorkshire, a favourite crossword river

explanation.surface: A stance adopted when in a difficult spot beside a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rough' turns SPOT into POST, which sits 'on' URE. 'Attitude' here is a physical stance.
explanation.definitionFit: An attitude can mean a bodily pose or stance, the way one holds oneself.

parts.note: Dis is the classical underworld, the city of hell in Dante
a charge is a fee for admission

explanation.surface: Asking about a very steep admission price, perhaps to the underworld.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pay' is the definition: to discharge a debt is to pay it off.
explanation.definitionFit: To discharge a debt or obligation is to settle it by payment.

clue.text: Like Tate or Fagin's sta pupil

definitions.meaning: the Tate gallery in London is full of art
in Oliver Twist the best of Fagin's young pickpockets is the Dodger, known by this nickname

explanation.definitionFit: Read as full of art it fits the Tate gallery, and it is the epithet of Dickens's pickpocket Jack Dawkins, the Dodger.

parts.note: re means about or concerning, as in business letters

indicators.note: poor suggests something in bad shape, so the letters of the dog's name are reworked

explanation.surface: Someone grasps what is going on concerning the unfortunate film dog Lassie.
explanation.definitionFit: To realise something is to grasp or become aware of it.

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the final letter of the word is cut off

parts.note: patrician means aristocratic, of the Roman noble class

explanation.surface: A young woman who is very nearly of aristocratic descent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost' drops the last N of PATRICIAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Patricia is a woman's first name.

indicators.note: first picks out the opening letter of the word before it

parts.note: rough can mean rowdy and boisterous

explanation.surface: Tom's first rowdy restaurant.
explanation.definitionFit: A trough is the container animals feed from, a farmyard dining spot.

clue.text: A good time to be a dissenter?

parts.note: taken as written
a no is a vote against, someone who dissents

explanation.surface: Asking whether it is a fine moment to become a rebel.
explanation.walkthrough: BE A NO: to be a 'no' vote.
explanation.definitionFit: Beano is British slang for a lively party or spree.

clue.text: Gay Regency dog at a stag party ?

parts.note: a buck was a fashionable young man about town in Regency England, a gay blade
a hound is a dog

explanation.surface: A Regency dandy behaving badly at a bachelor party.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'stag party' is a stag hunt, not a pre-wedding night out; the definition is the dog of the wordplay at such a hunt.
explanation.definitionFit: A buckhound is a hound bred for hunting deer, so it is found at a stag hunt.

clue.text: Maybe slips in a blunder we Aryans make

indicators.note: in tells us the letters are found inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: Slips of the tongue made in a gaffe by Aryans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Maybe' marks slips as one example of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Slips are women's undergarments, one kind of underclothing.

parts.note: wood is burnt as fuel
stock is a supply or store

explanation.surface: A new kind of fuel depot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel' looks like an adjective for new; it is a noun, Walter Scott's novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Woodstock is an 1826 historical novel by Sir Walter Scott.

clue.text: Lamp post one has to tolerate on a road

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits on top of the rest

parts.note: to stand something is to put up with it

explanation.surface: A street lamp is something you just have to put up with along a road.
explanation.definitionFit: A standard is an upright pole or post, and a standard lamp is a tall floor lamp.

indicators.note: teased means pulled apart, as wool is teased, so the letters are disentangled and rearranged

explanation.surface: A cat being taunted by someone called Leslie, the kind of description that suits paradise.
explanation.definitionFit: Celestial means heavenly, pertaining to the sky or paradise.

parts.note: in Greek legend a young man swam the Hellespont nightly to visit his beloved, a priestess called Hero

explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth this youth loved the priestess Hero and drowned crossing to her.

parts.note: joy is happiness
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A young woman brings joy to the congregation.
explanation.definitionFit: Joyce is a woman's first name.

indicators.note: to distress is to damage or knock about, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone is so upset they cannot hold back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Distress' looks like the subject but signals rearranging I with CANNOT.
explanation.definitionFit: To contain feelings is to hold them in check or keep them under control.

definitions.meaning: jumps a horse should take steadily, not charge at

explanation.definitionFit: A fence receives stolen goods, and fences are obstacles in showjumping that riders approach carefully.

parts.note: Hamlet greets his father's ghost asking whether it brings airs from paradise or blasts from hell

explanation.surface: A line from Hamlet with a word missing.
explanation.walkthrough: Fill in the missing word of Hamlet's speech to the Ghost in Act 1, Scene 4.
explanation.definitionFit: Hamlet's line contrasts airs from paradise with blasts from hell, the place of the blessed.

clue.text: But it's not a monotonous service

definitions.text: But it's not a monotonous service

parts.words: But it's not a monotonous service
parts.note: split in two the name suggests a song all on one level note, yet this church service is musical and varied

explanation.definitionFit: Evensong is the evening prayer service of the Anglican church, largely sung.

clue.text: One of the French not in time to wave

parts.note: un is French for one and du is French for of the
late means not punctual

explanation.surface: A Frenchman who is late arrives in time to wave.
explanation.definitionFit: To undulate is to move in waves, rising and falling.

clue.text: Honourable man or gangster, all sing in this music

parts.note: CH stands for Companion of Honour, a British order
taken as written
Al Capone, the Chicago gangster

explanation.surface: Whether a distinguished gentleman or a mobster, everyone joins in the singing here.
explanation.walkthrough: CH, Companion of Honour, is a British honour for distinguished service.
explanation.definitionFit: Choral music is written for a choir, where many voices sing together.

clue.text: Mildly cursed late return about the navy.

indicators.note: about means the turned word goes around the navy's letters
return means the word for late is read backwards

parts.note: late means dead, as in the late king
RN is the Royal Navy

explanation.surface: A late return from sea, mildly sworn at by the navy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return' turns DEAD into DAED, which goes 'about' RN.
explanation.definitionFit: Darned is a mild euphemism for damned, a soft oath.

clue.text: Tha's got wrong county — it's in USSR

indicators.note: got wrong means mixed up, so these letters are put in a new order

parts.note: the dialect contraction is just its four letters
Kent is a county in south-east England

explanation.surface: A Yorkshire voice telling someone they have the wrong county.
explanation.walkthrough: 'got wrong' rearranges THAS into TASH. Tha's is northern English dialect for 'you have'.
explanation.definitionFit: Tashkent is the capital of Uzbekistan, then a Soviet republic.
